events.verdict: Simpson (CHA) legally contests Harris' (DET) shot near the rim.
Hardaway Jr. (DET) holds Martin's (CHA) arm during the drive and the contact affects his SQBR.
Bridges (CHA) and Harris (DET) briefly engage and disengage as they pursue the rebound.
Duren (DET) is already in Martin's (CHA) path when contact occurs and he does not deliver contact during the pick.
Cunningham (DET) and Williams (CHA) briefly engage and disengage off-ball.
As Simpson (CHA) commits to going under the pick, Duren (DET) releases his screening position and marginal contact occurs as he rolls toward the basket.
Williams (CHA) applies his left forearm to Duren's (DET) upper body and marginal contact occurs as Williams deflects the ball away from Duren.
Duren (DET) reaches in and initiates contact with Green's (CHA) arm, which affects his driving shot attempt.
Bridges (CHA) does not maintain a legal guarding position and his arm initiates contact with Cunningham's (DET) arm that affects his driving shot attempt.
Williams (CHA) cleanly blocks Cunningham's (DET) shot attempt before the ball has reached its apex and started its downward flight towards the basket.
Duren (DET) is moving alongside Simpson's (CHA) path and his left forearm cleanly dislodges the ball from Simpson as he defends the driving shot attempt.
Green (CHA) commits a take foul on Thompson (DET).  Coach Bickerstaff's (DET) request for a timeout is not recognized by the crew prior to the foul call.
Bridges (CHA) avoids entering the lane prior to the shot being released.

As Bridges (CHA) cuts back towards the lane, he moves back into Thompson's (DET) extended left forearm, which causes contact to Bridges' head/neck.  Contact to an opponent's head/face can be deemed marginal when the result of a natural basketball move, provided the contact is not disproportionate or uncontrolled.
Thompson (DET) legally contests Bridges' (CHA) jump shot attempt.
Williams (CHA) extends his arms and delivers contact to Hardaway Jr. (DET) that dislodges him from his offensive position.
